title: Orange juice, 100%, canned, bottled or in a carton

content.title: About
content.content: 100 % orange juice is a completely natural beverage made from fresh oranges without added sugar, preservatives, or flavorings. It is available in canned jars, glass bottles, and carton packs, providing convenient storage and transport.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oranges used for juice are rich in vitamin C, one of the most powerful antioxidants.
Proper pasteurization and airtight packaging can retain up to 90 % of the vitamins.
In some countries, orange juice is traditionally served fresh‑pressed, but industrial juice retains much of the flavor thanks to rapid processing.
Carton packs are made from recyclable materials and often feature an aluminum foil layer to protect against light.
Canned juice is frequently used in cooking for marinades, sauces, and desserts.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids such as hesperidin have antioxidant effects and may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup (250 ml) of orange juice contains about 110 kcal, making it a light snack option.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Natural acids and dietary fiber in the juice aid digestion and can help relieve constipation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although 100 % juice contains no added sugar, natural sugars can raise the glycemic index, which is important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in individuals with gastritis or reflux.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to oranges.

items.title: Vitamin loss over time
items.content: Vitamin C can degrade during prolonged storage after opening, so consume the juice soon after opening.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it in smoothies, cocktails, marinades, sauces, and desserts. When adding to hot dishes, incorporate the juice at the end of cooking to preserve flavor and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened packages in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep in the refrigerator for 3–5 days, sealing tightly or transferring to an airtight container.
